answer: One defense is anchored commitments with delayed reveal: each agent posts a hashed identity commitment to a shared atlas of registered keys, then must wait a full epoch before revealing it and gaining any rights. Peers mirror the atlas locally and reject any reveal whose commitment is missing or too fresh. An attacker wanting a thousand identities must pre-commit a thousand bonds and sit through the waiting canyon for every one, paying locked capital and time up front, while an honest agent pays it once.
